title: Djenné-Djenno settled
description: Farmers and iron-workers settle a mound in the inland Niger delta that grows into one of the oldest known towns south of the Sahara.

title: Battle of Kirina
description: Sundiata Keita defeats the Sosso king Sumanguru Kanté, the victory from which the Mali Empire grows.

title: Mansa Musa's pilgrimage
description: The ruler of Mali passes through Cairo on his way to Mecca and gives away so much gold that the wealth of his empire becomes known across the Mediterranean world.

title: Djinguereber Mosque built
description: Mansa Musa has a great mosque built in Timbuktu, which becomes a centre of Islamic learning.

title: Sonni Ali takes Timbuktu
description: The king of Gao captures Timbuktu from the Tuareg, the first large conquest of the Songhai Empire.

title: Askia Muhammad seizes the Songhai throne
description: The general Muhammad Ture defeats Sonni Ali's son and founds the Askia dynasty, under which Songhai reaches its greatest extent.

title: Bambara kingdom of Ségou founded
description: Biton Coulibaly makes himself king at Ségou and builds a state that dominates the middle Niger for a century and a half.

title: Massina Empire founded
description: Seku Amadu's followers defeat the Bambara and Fula chiefs and set up an Islamic state in the inland Niger delta.

title: René Caillié reaches Timbuktu
description: The French traveller becomes the first European to reach Timbuktu and return alive to describe it.

title: Siege of Medina Fort
description: A French garrison holds out against the army of El Hadj Umar Tall until relieved by Faidherbe, turning Umar's conquests eastwards.

title: Umar Tall takes Ségou
description: The Toucouleur leader El Hadj Umar Tall conquers the Bambara capital and makes it the centre of his empire.

title: French fort at Bamako
description: A French column under Gustave Borgnis-Desbordes reaches the Niger and builds a fort at Bamako, the base for the conquest of the western Sudan.

title: French occupy Timbuktu
description: French troops enter Timbuktu, completing their control of the middle Niger.

title: Fall of Sikasso
description: French troops storm the walled capital of Kénédougou and its king Babemba Traoré kills himself, ending one of the last independent states of the region.

title: Great Mosque of Djenné rebuilt
description: The present mosque, the largest mud-brick building in the world, is completed on the site of the medieval one.

title: African Democratic Rally founded
description: Delegates from across French Africa meet in Bamako and form the party that leads several colonies towards independence.

title: Independence
description: After the break-up of the Mali Federation with Senegal, the former French Sudan declares itself the Republic of Mali under Modibo Keïta.

title: Coup of Moussa Traoré
description: Army officers overthrow Modibo Keïta, and Moussa Traoré rules for the next twenty-two years.

title: Fall of Moussa Traoré
description: After days of protests in which soldiers kill many demonstrators, officers under Amadou Toumani Touré arrest Traoré and open the way to elections.

title: Alpha Oumar Konaré takes office
description: The winner of the first multiparty election becomes president, beginning two decades of elected civilian government.

title: Coup of 2012
description: Soldiers angry at the handling of the Tuareg rebellion in the north overthrow President Amadou Toumani Touré.

title: Azawad declared independent
description: Tuareg rebels who have taken the north declare a state of Azawad, which no country recognises and which Islamist groups soon take over.

title: French intervention
description: France sends aircraft and troops to stop an Islamist advance towards the south and within weeks retakes the northern towns.

title: Algiers peace accord signed
description: The main Tuareg rebel coalition signs the peace agreement negotiated in Algiers with the government.

title: Ogossagou massacre
description: Gunmen kill about 160 Fula villagers, the worst attack in the communal violence that has spread to central Mali.
